Beacon https://beaconsoftware.com is building the essential technology infrastructure for the everyday economy: the businesses, organizations, and services that make real life work, and that mainstream tech has largely left behind. We acquire, operate, and grow vertical market software companies. They are niche, founder-built businesses serving industries that are often overlooked and too profitable to ignore.

Our model is simple: we seek out founders who have built their business by spending years understanding their market and prioritizing their customers' specific needs. We buy great businesses, invest in their continued growth, and hold them permanently, accelerating that growth with an AI-native platform built specifically for vertical market software. No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

We are not a financial firm. We are technology entrepreneurs and operators who believe the most important businesses in the world are already running quietly in industries most people never think about. Our job is to find them, support the people who built them, and make them better.

Beacon is backed by a diverse base of investors, with $550M+ raised to date, including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp, and evergreen funds built for the long game.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Deal Origination Associate, you will play a critical role in Beacon's acquisition strategy by identifying, researching, and engaging directly with software companies to join the Beacon family. You will work closely with Beacon's leadership and M&A teams to support the entire deal process—from initial outreach to deal closing. This is a unique opportunity to help shape the future of Beacon's growing portfolio of software companies.



RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Identify niche vertical market software companies aligned with Beacon's acquisition strategy.

 - Conduct outreach through email, phone calls, and meetings to engage with company founders and CEOs.

 - Build and nurture long-term relationships with software entrepreneurs, understanding their business challenges and growth opportunities.

 - Assist in the initial evaluation of potential acquisition targets by gathering and analyzing financial and operational data.

 - Maintain and grow Beacon's deal pipeline by actively sourcing new business opportunities.

 - Collaborate with Beacon's M&A and leadership teams throughout the due diligence and deal execution process.

 - Support deal negotiations by coordinating communication between internal stakeholders and prospective sellers.
   


QUALIFICATIONS:

 - A driven, proactive individual with 1-3 years of experience in M&A business development, sales, or a related field, ideally in the software or technology sector.

 - Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage and influence entrepreneurs and business leaders.

 - Love the sales process and are genuinely interested in getting to know people and are intellectually curious about entrepreneurship/business. 

 - Analytical with an attention to detail, and eager to learn about acquisitions and deal-making in the software industry.

 - Excellent written and oral communication skills. 

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and managing multiple projects simultaneously.

 - A self-starter who thrives in a collaborative team environment and is passionate about achieving/exceeding targets. 

 - Experience in outreach, relationship-building, or lead generation.

 - A basic understanding of financial statements, SaaS business models, or M&A processes.

 - Interest in software, technology, and the broader acquisition ecosystem.
   


WHAT YOU WILL GET FROM BEACON:

 - Dedicated mentor.

 - Demonstrated interest in learning about different businesses across diverse industries.

 - Learn directly from entrepreneurs who have scaled businesses from seed-to-$10B+ IPOs.

 - Work directly with Silicon Valley product and engineering teams to perform diligence and underwrite technology driven value creation streams with potential acquisitions.

 - Operate in an environment that encourages initiative and rapid development.

 - Strong development of interpersonal and presentation skills.

 - Unique work environment which combines a high growth technology startup and a long term buy/hold private equity investment firm.


Our Values at Beacon Software

 - Humility: We acknowledge that the path to getting to the right answer involves being wrong along the way. We have strong beliefs which are weakly held. We actively seek new ideas and believe we can learn from anyone at any time.

 - Honesty: We are truth seeking in our approach to business problems. Business is a repeat game and we believe that human relationships generate alpha. We understand that trust is earned over a lifetime and can be lost in an instant.

 - Hunger: We play to win. We hold ourselves to high standards and will not be outworked. We take pride in having a deep sense of responsibility to ourselves, each other, our partners, and our customers. We believe to whom much is given much is expected.

 - Horizon: We seek to build a generational software company. This will take decades. We manage our expectations and those of our partners to take advantage of the 8th wonder of the world - compounding growth.


How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process: To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Beacon Software uses Artificial Intelligence and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.

 

AI does not make hiring decisions: Every application is reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

About the Role
 Our client is seeking a Senior AWS DataHub Developer to design and build real-time, event-driven data services on AWS. This role is developer-first (application-side) rather than infrastructure-led. You will architect and deliver Kafka-based streaming pipelines and serverless data applications that ingest, transform, and serve data at scale.
 You’ll collaborate with architects, data engineers, and product teams to deliver secure, resilient, observable, and highly scalable solutions that power enterprise-grade analytics and event-driven applications.
 What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities)
 Design & Deliver Event-Driven Pipelines: Build serverless data flows using AWS Lambda, Step Functions, EventBridge, SNS, SQS, API Gateway.
 Real-Time Streaming: Develop Kafka (Apache Kafka/Amazon MSK) consumers/producers for high-throughput, low-latency streaming and decoupled microservices.
 Microservices & APIs: Build and optimize TypeScript (preferred) or Python services/APIs for data ingestion, transformation, and delivery.
 AWS Data Services Integration: Work with S3, DynamoDB, Glue, Athena, CloudWatch for storage, metadata, querying, and observability.
 Quality & Reliability: Implement idempotency, retries, dead-letter queues, exactly-once/at-least-once semantics where appropriate, and schema evolution strategies.
 CI/CD & Testing: Use Git-based workflows and CI/CD (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins) with automated tests (unit/integration/load) and infrastructure deployments.
 IaC (Developer View): Define application-layer infrastructure using AWS CDK, Terraform, or CloudFormation—with strong emphasis on developer productivity and repeatability.
 Agile Collaboration: Contribute to technical design, story sizing, peer reviews, and continuous improvement.
 Ideal Candidate Profile
 You are a cloud-native, application-side developer who thinks in events, streams, and services—not servers. You design for resiliency, observability, and scale, and you’re comfortable pairing Kafka with AWS serverless to deliver business outcomes.

 The Intake Worker is responsible for providing a welcoming, safe, and supportive first point of contact for youth who are experiencing homelessness, are at immediate risk of homelessness, or require housing-related assistance. Working within a trauma-informed, youth-centered, Housing First for Youth-aligned approach, the Intake Worker responds to all inquiries for services, completes initial screenings and gathering of call data, ensures accurate and timely documentation, identifies immediate safety concerns that require timely escalation, and coordinates access to emergency shelter, diversion, homelessness prevention, and community-based supports.
 HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT  🎯
 Central Intake and Initial Response 
 Serve as a central point of contact for youth seeking emergency shelter, housing assistance, transitional housing access, diversion services or other supports.
 Provide timely response to inquiries and referrals by telephone, email, in person and through designated referral systems.
 Gather relevant information regarding the youth’s immediate circumstances, housing status, presenting needs and current level of risk.
 Maintain accurate call logs and wait lists, as required.
 Provide consistent, accurate, relevant, and timely information in all communications and data sets to support and inform decision-making.
 In consultation with the Diversion team, determine the urgency of each request and prioritize response based on safety, vulnerability and immediate housing needs.
 Screening, Assessment and Service Planning 
 Initiate the Diversion Assessment process for youth seeking shelter, and gather initial information about the caller, as required per intake and triage protocol.
 Document the youth’s immediate shelter and housing needs, including where the youth stayed previously and where they may be able to safely stay that evening.
 Identify immediate risks related to violence, abuse, human trafficking, mental health, substance use, medical needs, wand other identified risk factors.
 Provide required information to prevention team as required for accurate and timely decision-making, as per youth assignment protocol.
 Information, Referral and Service Navigation 
 Provide relevant referral information about shelter, housing, income, mental health, substance use, health, legal, education, employment, and community services to address the presenting issues of the caller
 Facilitate warm referrals whenever possible rather than only providing contact information.

 Develop and maintain effective working relationships with community partners and referral sources.

 Provide a welcoming, respectful, non-judgmental and youth-friendly response to all individuals seeking assistance.
 Consult with supervisors or appropriate clinical, crisis or emergency services when elevated risks are identified.

 Document inquiries, referrals, admissions, unsuccessful contacts, interventions, and service outcomes.

 Maintain professional and collaborative relationships with youth, colleagues, families, community partners and referral sources.
 Follow organizational policies, collective-agreement requirements, health-and-safety practices and professional standards.
 All other duties as required.

DO YOU WANT TO SUPPORT JOBBERINO'S TO DO THEIR BEST WORK?

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a People Business Partner to be part of our People department.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=24.

The team:

The People team builds the environment where Jobberinos do their best work: how people are hired, onboarded, grown, paid, and supported when life gets complicated.

We are a small team, which means a lot of ground to cover and real ownership of it. You are closely embedded in the business and find out quickly when something worked. You’ll work at two altitudes: strategic (the diagnosis and the advice) and execution (the documentation and the follow-through that makes it better next time). AI is how we cover both, and we are rebuilding the way this team works around it rather than running it as a side project.

The role:

Reporting to the Senior Manager, People, the People Business Partner is an intermediate level role embedded in a business unit, and the person leaders go to when they need both practical and strategic support. You adapt frameworks to the situation in front of you, and where there is no precedent, you build the approach. You work independently and check in on the decisions that matter.

This is a hands-on role at both ends of the range. You will partner directly with the senior leaders and executives who run your group, bringing them a recommendation rather than a question. You will spend time coaching managers who are leading people for the first time, becoming their essential partner as they learn, and you will also spend real time on leave administration, performance documentation, and employee relations case management. This role provides a great balance for someone who wants both the strategy and the execution.

You will build for where Jobber is going, not just where it is. Structures will change, manager expectations will shift, and AI will change what a team can do. With your strong business knowledge, you will bring forward your viewpoint to influence the department's health and success.

The People Business Partner will: 

 - Know your group's strategy, structure, and drivers well enough to build a people agenda that gets ahead of capability, engagement, retention, and succession risk.

 - Advise managers and senior leaders across performance, development, compensation, team structure, and change. Communicate for leaders who do not know People, and persuade where you need to.

 - Coach first-time and early-tenure managers through the hard parts of people leadership. Leaving them more capable and equipped to lead afterward.

 - Identify when the same question keeps returning, and build the guidance once to multiply your impact and allow managers to be self-sufficient.

 - Run performance management end to end: expectations, documentation standards, improvement plans, and the difficult conversations and exits that follow.

 - Bring judgment to talent review and compensation cycles: calibration, leveling, promotions, and succession gaps named before someone resigns.

 - Own the employee lifecycle for your group: leaves, accommodations, return to work, internal moves, and exits, including the administration and coordination with managers, payroll, and providers that keeps it accurate and humane.

 - Manage employee relations independently, including ambiguous and legally sensitive cases, with a firm grip on employment legislation and clear escalation when it is warranted.

 - Assess structures, spans of control, and decision rights when performance or growth raises structural questions. Identify a people problem from a design problem, and support leaders through the changes that follow.

 - Track leading indicators across engagement, performance, and retention, run your group's listening cycles, and turn results into action plans leaders commit to.

 - Drive people initiatives end to end. Adapt an existing program where one fits, build the approach where nothing does.

 - Use AI in the work, not around it. Delegate research and drafting to agents so your time goes to judgment, analyze your group's data to arrive at leadership conversations with a point of view, and pressure test your recommendations before you take them forward.

 - Bring forward the gaps. When a manual process or documentation hole keeps generating the same escalation, propose what should replace it.

 - Partner with Talent Development, Total Rewards, and Talent Attraction so your group gets one answer, not three. Stay current on where People practice and tech are heading, and bring what works back to the PBP team, because the pattern you found almost always exists elsewhere.

To be successful, you should have:

 - A proven track record of advising and influencing senior leaders and executives, including the ones who needed persuading and who did not arrive with the problem framed. Ideally somewhere that was growing while you were there.

 - Performance management and employee relations experience you can speak to specifically, including the cases that did not go the way you planned.

 - Experience running performance and compensation cycles end to end for a multi-team group, not supporting someone else's.

 - A working understanding of employment legislation and how it applies to our business. When we expand into new regions, you get yourself up to speed quickly.

 - Real AI fluency. You can point to work you do differently now than a year ago, and to something you have built or automated yourself.

 - Comfort with the administrative side. Getting the documentation, systems, and detail right matters to the person on the other end.

 - Credibility that comes from following through. You do what you say, which is why leaders trust you with the hard things.

 - Strong written and verbal communication. You can prepare a brief for leadership and deliver content at a department All Hands.

 - The resilience to keep moving when the situation is messy and the answer is not obvious yet.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $98,300, a midpoint of $115,700, and a maximum salary of $133,100, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual’s current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

Location: 

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!
